title: Handing Over
logline: Nirala does not run from her handcuffs: he asks to hand over charge first. Pushpa admits she sent every complainant the SHO refused across the line, and that the SHO has known for two years. From inside the ticket-booth lockup Nandini watches Bhaiyaji hand his 'Inspector sahab' the month's envelope, and watches Nirala seal it as case property: the twenty-fourth. She gives him until ten tomorrow. That evening the SHO learns she is reading the files, and dials Bhaiyaji.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast as the Hinglish cut; 'thana', 'madam', 'sahab', 'ji' and 'lockup' kept as spoken in India.
script_note: Indian English adaptation of script.hi.json, not a literal translation. Spoken text is subtitle text with the square-bracket tags removed.

characters.name: Nandini Joshi
characters.role: LEAD. Sub-Inspector, six weeks into her first posting. Ordered to have the fake Inspector in her lockup before ten tomorrow.
characters.look: Indian woman, 28, tall (about 170 cm), lean, very straight-backed. Medium-brown skin, oval face, straight thick black eyebrows, level dark-brown eyes, firm mouth. Black hair, clean centre parting, low ponytail to the shoulder blades. No make-up, no bindi, no jewellery, no watch. Approved force uniform, crisp: sandy khaki shirt, two buttoned chest pockets, full sleeves; dark teal epaulettes with TWO off-white bars; white lantern on a round teal patch on each upper sleeve; khaki trousers; black belt with a black handcuff pouch on her right hip; black shoes; blue ballpoint pen clipped in her left chest pocket. No cap, no stars. Cherry-red open-face scooter helmet: on the lobby bench from s2e01 b10 until b5 of this episode, then held against her chest in the booth (b6), then under her left arm (b8, b10).
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, late twenties, clear mid-range voice. Indian English with a neutral educated small-city north-Indian accent; not British, not American. Keeps 'madam', 'thana', 'lockup', 'sahab', 'ji'. Quick, clipped. Under pressure she gets quieter, slower and more exact, never louder. Dry, not sarcastic.

characters.name: Sudhir Nirala
characters.role: Calls himself Inspector. Former booking clerk of the shut Roopam Talkies; runs a thana of his own in its lobby. The town calls him 'Nirala ji'; only Bhaiyaji calls him 'Inspector sahab'.
characters.look: Indian man, 40, slight and short (about 160 cm), narrow sloping shoulders, thin neck. Light-brown skin, long narrow face, large earnest eyes, neat black pencil moustache. Home-stitched copy of the force uniform, over-starched and ONE SIZE TOO BIG: shoulder seams droop, sleeves end at his knuckles, collar stands away from his neck, belt tail hangs loose. Teal epaulettes with three off-white bars; lantern sleeve patches. THE ONLY PEAKED CAP IN THE SERIES: khaki, teal band, shiny black peak, no badge, dead level. One large home-made medal above his left chest pocket: a blank brass-yellow disc as wide as his palm on a broad maroon-and-off-white striped ribbon. Brown leather holster with a buttoned flap on his right hip, never opened in this episode. Rubber stamp and tin ink pad from his right trouser pocket.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, forty, light careful tenor. Careful, slightly old-fashioned small-town north-Indian English, as learnt from manuals ('kindly', 'one does not'); English police terms pronounced with great care; not British, not American. Complete sentences, no contractions. Unhurried, courteous, never raises his voice, never jokes: the comedy is that he means it. Frightened is a thin, steady voice, not a stammer. Says 'madam' at the end of sentences.

characters.name: Pushpa Kumari
characters.role: Head Constable, twenty-six years at the Imlipur thana. Sent every complainant the SHO refused across the line.
characters.look: Indian woman, 50, short (about 152 cm) and solid. Wheat-brown skin, round face, sharp small eyes over round steel-rimmed spectacles worn low. Grey-streaked black hair in a tight high bun with TWO STEEL KNITTING NEEDLES pushed through it in a cross. Approved uniform, teal epaulettes with ONE off-white bar, lantern patches. Hand-knitted plum-purple cardigan over it, open, two sagging pockets, a ball of orange wool in the right pocket. Cloth knitting bag over her left shoulder outdoors. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, fifty, low, dry, even alto. Plain, unhurried small-town Indian English with a clear Hindi accent; not British, not American. Short sentences; keeps 'madam', 'SHO sahab'. Says the important thing in the fewest words and goes back to her knitting. Never surprised. Warmth shows only as dryness.

characters.name: Balram 'Bhaiyaji' Thakur
characters.role: Runs the ration godown and most of Imlipur. Pays the talkies 'outpost' every month and believes it is his. Called only 'Bhaiyaji' in this episode.
characters.look: Indian man, 45, broad and solid, about 178 cm, thick neck, big square hands. Brown skin, thick black hair combed straight back, full black moustache, an unhurried closed-lip smile as his resting face. Spotless white cotton kurta, sleeves pushed up, white pyjama trousers, brown leather sandals. Heavy gold watch on his LEFT wrist. Dark sunglasses pushed up on top of his head, never over his eyes. A fat ring of godown keys hooked on his RIGHT index finger, swinging.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, mid-forties, warm, low, smiling voice. Soft, hospitable small-town north-Indian English with a strong Hindi accent; not British, not American. Keeps 'Inspector sahab', 'Tripathi ji'. Courteous to the point of menace; never threatens, never hurries, laughs before he says the worst thing.

characters.name: Dayashankar Tripathi
characters.role: Inspector, SHO Imlipur. Two years without an FIR and a zero-crime shield for it. Has known about the fake thana for two years.
characters.look: Indian man, 56, large, heavy and slow, about 175 cm, big soft belly. Warm-brown skin, bald dome with a grey fringe at the sides, heavy jowls, clean-shaven, half-closed sleepy eyes. Approved uniform worn slack: khaki half-sleeve shirt, top two buttons open over a white vest, teal epaulettes with three off-white bars, lantern patches. Red-and-white checked gamchha over his LEFT shoulder. A paper cone of roasted peanuts in his LEFT hand, shells on the desk. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, mid-fifties, deep, slow, comfortable baritone, often speaking round a mouthful. Slow eastern-UP Indian English with a heavy Hindi accent, never crisp; not British, not American. Avuncular and lazy. Under pressure he stops chewing and goes flat and low; he does not shout.

characters.name: A neighbour (voice only)
characters.role: One of the two neighbours in the bicycle dispute (token eight). Never a face: on screen the two neighbours are two pairs of hands on one handlebar. One line, called up the stair.
characters.look: Not seen as a face. Hands only: a man's forearm in a faded blue shirt sleeve gripping the handlebar.
characters.voice_note: Middle-aged male, small-town Indian accent, calling up a stair from the lobby: carrying, friendly, not a shout. The line is a name and is said exactly as in the Hinglish cut; the Hinglish take may be reused. Gender is the casting director's call if the hands are redrawn.

location: Imlipur: the projection room of the shut Roopam Talkies (b1, b2), the talkies lobby that is Nirala's thana (b3 to b10), and the real Imlipur thana in the evening (b11, b12).
time_of_day: Day 1. About 2 p.m. in the projection room, seconds after s2e01 ends (b1, b2); afternoon in the lobby, Bhaiyaji arriving at about 4 p.m. (b3 to b10), the light through the high windows lower and warmer from b6; about 7 p.m. in the real thana, one tube light (b11, b12). Clocks in frame have hands and no numerals.

beats.action: OPENS IN THE SAME ROOM SECONDS AFTER s2e01, no recap. Afternoon light in shafts from the one small window; steel racks of sealed brown envelopes and cloth-tied files; the old projector under its dust sheet. Shot 1, l01 (the hook, inside the first second): tight on Nandini's right hand resting on the black handcuff pouch on her right hip, where s2e01 left it, token seven's string still looped round that wrist, the grey cardboard token hanging below it; behind it, soft, the red-cloth file lies open on the stool. Shot 2, l02: Nirala, medium close, cap dead level, medal on his chest; his eyes go from her hand to the open file and back; he does not step back. Shot 3, l03: Nandini, waist up; on this line her right hand draws the steel cuffs out of the pouch (D-016 direction 10: the cuffs come out here, not before) while her left hand pockets token seven, its string slipped off her right wrist: in the still, cuffs in her right hand, that wrist bare, the end of the string going into her left trouser pocket. Shot 4, l04: Nirala, same set-up as shot 2. Pushpa is in the room by the racks but is seen only as her hands, knitting stopped, at the edge of shot 1: no third face in any frame. STATE: token seven on its string round her right wrist until l03, then in her left trouser pocket for the rest of the episode (not seen again); cuffs in Nandini's right hand from l03 to b10; her helmet is downstairs on the lobby bench.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] Arrest is your right, madam.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] But one does not leave a thana without charge handover.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [sharply] Charge handover of a fake thana?

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [quietly] The thana is fake. The complaints are real.

beats.action: THE SET-UP, AS A FOUR-LINE EXCHANGE (key line 4 split at its sentence break). Nandini turns from him to Pushpa. Singles and one two-shot; Nirala stays in the room, out of frame. Shot 1, l05: Nandini, cuffs hanging from her right hand. Shot 2, l06: Pushpa by the racks, spectacles low, winding orange wool off the ball, not looking up. Shot 3, l07: Nandini. Shot 4, l08 to the word 'shield': Pushpa, the wool still; on 'shield' cut to an insert from the real_thana plate: the zero-crime shield on the wall, its brass plate painted blank. Shot 5, l09: two-shot, Nandini picture-left, Pushpa picture-right; Pushpa's needles start again. Nothing here says that Bhaiyaji pays the talkies: b6 to b8 show it first.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [flatly] You knew.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [calm] I sent them, madam. Whoever SHO sahab turned away, across the line.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [sharply] And SHO sahab?

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [calm] He's known for two years. If he speaks up, the shield goes.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [sighs] So he never told the department. Or Bhaiyaji.

beats.action: The talkies lobby, dusty light from the high windows. Shot 1, silence then l10: from the lobby floor looking up the back stair: Nirala coming down first, Nandini a step behind him with the cuffs in her right hand. Foreground picture-right, at the complainants' bench: two pairs of hands gripping one bicycle handlebar between them, a grey cardboard token on a string looped over one wrist (overlay ov_token_8: '8'); her red helmet lies on the bench beside them. The call comes from the bench, off frame; the neighbours are never faces. Shot 2, l11: Nirala at the foot of the stair, turning to her with a small courteous nod, excusing himself.

lines.speaker: neighbour_voice
lines.text: Nirala ji!

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] Token eight.

beats.action: He settles it from his own register at the desk (the old booking counter); the two pairs of hands on the handlebar at the desk's edge. Shot 1, l12: insert, top-down: his pen at an older page of his register, a finger under one entry (painted blank; the number is spoken); he says it aloud as he writes it on a fresh receipt. Shot 2, silent inside the speaker gap: one of the two hands lets go of the handlebar. The stamp coming down and the receipt tearing off are sound under the end of shot 2. Shot 3, l13: Nirala looking up at her, the torn receipt in his hand. Shot 4, l14: Nandini by a pillar, cuffs in her right hand, eyes lifting to the lobby wall clock; insert of the clock, hands and no numerals (D-016 direction 17), from which she has timed him.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] Frame nine-two-seven. On record.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [earnest] Whatever you write, say it aloud, madam. So that the witness hears.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] Ten minutes flat.

beats.action: The receipt is still in his hand when a car door shuts outside (sound, in the silence before the line). Shot 1, l15 up to 'Madam...': Nirala at the desk, gone completely still, eyes on the lobby door. Shot 2, from 'lockup में': his free hand pointing past her at the ticket booth with its arched grille; Nandini at the picture-left edge, already reaching for her red helmet on the bench. The neighbours' hands are gone from the handlebar.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [nervous] Bhaiyaji. Madam... the lockup. I mean... kindly hide.

beats.action: COMIC IMAGE. Shot 1, held in silence: the ticket booth from the front: in the arched grille window, the real Sub-Inspector's eyes, her red helmet clutched against her chest with both arms, the cuffs hanging from her right hand over it. Nothing of hers is left on the desk or the bench. Shot 2, l16: the desk from the lobby side: Bhaiyaji, broad and unhurried, keys swinging from his right index finger, laying a brown envelope on the desk; Nirala picture-left in three-quarter back, Bhaiyaji picture-right, face to camera. Shot 3, l17 first sentence: same two-shot, Bhaiyaji's left hand (the gold watch) opening at the room. Shot 4, l17 from the laugh: the grille again, her eyes wider. Never more than two faces in a frame.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [chuckles] Inspector sahab! This month's.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [calm] Our outpost, our Inspector sahab. [laughs] Cheaper than Tripathi ji, and sweeter.

beats.action: Shot 1, l18: Bhaiyaji leaning on the counter, closer, smiling. Shot 2, l19: Nirala picking the envelope up in both hands, sleeves over his knuckles. Shot 3, silence after the lines: Bhaiyaji's left index finger flicking the brass medal on Nirala's chest; the disc tilted on its ribbon. He goes: the keys' jingle is the last thing out of the door, as sound running into b8. Nandini is in the booth throughout, out of these frames.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [quietly] Those thirty papers... still asleep, no?

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] In the file, Bhaiyaji.

beats.action: MERGED BEAT (old b8 and b9; there is no b9). Shot 1, l20: Nandini stepping out of the booth, helmet now under her left arm, cuffs in her right hand; at the desk Nirala is already writing on the envelope, aloud. Shot 2, l21: Nandini across the desk. Shot 3, l22: Nirala, pen lifted. Shot 4, l23: insert: a blob of red wax on the envelope flap and a blank tag tied on (overlay ov_envelope_tag: a date and a serial number; the line carries it). Shot 5, l24: insert: the malkhana ledger open on the desk with the new entry written; her right index finger, the open cuffs hanging from the same hand across the page, has gone down the column of entries and stops on the last one. Shot 6, l25: Nirala, close, cap level, the sealed envelope flat under his hand. All in the lobby: the racks upstairs are not revisited.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] Note seven-seven-three...

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [sharply] You took a bribe.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [earnest] Taking a bribe is a crime. Seizing it is duty.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] This is case property.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [flatly] Twenty-four.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [quietly] For two years I have waited for a real officer to ask for them.

beats.action: Still at the desk; the light through the high windows lower. Pushpa has come down the stair behind them and waits at its foot with her knitting bag: a back and a bun with two crossed needles, never a third face in frame. Shot 1, l26: Nandini. Shot 2, l27: Nirala, plain, no self-pity, hands flat on the register. Shot 3, l28: insert: her right hand putting the cuffs back into the pouch on her hip and snapping the flap shut. Shot 4, l29 and l30: two-shot across the desk, Nandini picture-left, Nirala picture-right. Shot 5, silence after the lines: Pushpa's back in the bright lobby doorway, going out, sent back across the line to watch the thana (Nandini's tilt of the head at the door is the cue; no line).

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Why didn't you join the police?

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] Nine times. Every time, my chest measured one centimetre short.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [quietly] It takes no chest to hear a complaint.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Before ten tomorrow, in my lockup.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] Till then, do your charge handover.

beats.action: Evening, the real thana, one tube light, the ceiling fan turning (sound). Shot 1, l31: Tripathi at his desk under the zero-crime shield, the paper cone of peanuts in his left hand, gamchha on his left shoulder, mouth full. Shot 2, l32: Pushpa back at the side table with her knitting, not looking up. Shot 3, silence after the lines: close on Tripathi: he has stopped chewing, a peanut halfway to his mouth. Shot 4, silence: Pushpa going out of the doorway, slowly, his empty tea glass in her hand: he has sent her for tea without a word.

lines.speaker: tripathi
lines.text: [calm] So, arrest done?

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [deadpan] No, SHO sahab. Madam is reading the files.

beats.action: ENDING, SPOKEN. Tripathi alone under the shield; the complainants' bench by the door empty. Shot 1, silence: he wipes his right hand on the gamchha; the door by the empty bench, the one Pushpa went out of, left a hand's width open (Pushpa not shown). Shot 2, silence: the black desk phone, his hand on the lifted receiver, the coiled cord; the last two digits, one short ring-back burst and the click of a pick-up are sound. Shot 3, l33: close on his mouth and the receiver. Shot 4, l34: tighter on his mouth, the shield soft behind. Cut to black on the last word, before any answer.

lines.speaker: tripathi
lines.text: [quietly] Bhaiyaji? Tripathi speaking.

lines.speaker: tripathi
lines.text: [quietly] Had to tell you one thing... about that talkies outpost.

sfx_notes: b1-b2 bed: the projection room's dry quiet, a faint street outside the small window, dust; Pushpa's needles silent in b1, clicking again from the end of b2.
b1 l03: the snap of the pouch flap and the clink of steel cuffs drawn out, close and dry.
b2: wool pulling off the ball under l06; needles resume under l09.
b3: footsteps on the wooden stair; a bicycle bell gives one small tring as the two hands tug the handlebar, before l10.
b4: pen scratch under l12; between l12 and l13 the stamp comes down (one dry wooden thump) and the receipt tears off along its perforation; the lobby wall clock ticking under l14.
b5: outside, a car door shuts, solid and heavy, then nothing; sandals on gravel coming closer under l15.
b6: sandals on terrazzo; the ring of keys jingling on his finger; a paper envelope laid on wood. Keep the keys light under l17 so the laugh and the line stay clear.
b7: a small brass tink as he flicks the medal; the keys' jingle walks out of the door and fades into the start of b8.
b8: the booth grille door creaking under l20; pen on paper; a match struck and wax dripping under l23; a ledger page turned under l24.
b10: the cuffs going into the pouch and the flap snapping shut under l28; Pushpa's steps on terrazzo out of the door after l30.
b11 bed: tube-light hum and a slow ceiling fan; peanut shells cracking under l31; needles under l32. On the stopped-chewing shot every sound but the fan drops out.

b12: inside the 1.8 s hold: receiver lifted (plastic clack), the last two digits dialled, one short ring-back burst (not a full ring cadence), a click as it is picked up. No phone filter: we hear Tripathi's side in the room. Bhaiyaji's voice is never heard. The fan and any bed duck right down under l33 and l34 so the cliffhanger is fully intelligible; hard cut to silence on the last word.
music_note: Mostly dry. b3-b4: a light plucked procedural motif (a single string instrument, deadpan, a few notes per bar) under the bicycle dispute, gone at the car door in b5. b6-b7: one low, warm sustained note under Bhaiyaji, faintly uneasy, out when the keys leave. b8: nothing but sound. b10: a soft single sustained chord enters under l28 and resolves under l30. b11: no music. b12: a low drone enters with the ring-back, ducks under both lines and cuts to silence with the picture on the last word. Instrumental, no melody hook, no percussion hits, no comic stings.
ending_question: What did Tripathi tell Bhaiyaji about the talkies outpost, and what will Bhaiyaji now do to the man he believes is the Inspector he bought?
writer_notes: English adaptation of script.hi.json (S5), not a literal translation. Same beats (b1 to b8, b10 to b12; no b9, as in the Hindi), same line ids l01 to l34, same speakers, same order, same silent_seconds and silent_position per beat, and every emotion tag of the Hindi line kept in the same position. Only text, the per-line target_seconds and the descriptive fields (title, logline, names, voice_note, ending_question) differ. action, on_screen, location, sfx_notes and music_note are copied unchanged: picture and sound are shared between the two cuts. Sources: content/series2/bible.json (voice_by_language.en for each principal, names_rule, title.en 'Handing Over', the 'outpost' wording, Bhaiyaji's sample line used verbatim in l16) read with D-004, D-006, D-016, D-008, D-013 and D-014.

Register: Nandini clipped and dry, keeps 'thana', 'madam', 'lockup', 'SHO sahab'. Nirala in manual English with no contractions ('one does not leave a thana', 'kindly hide', 'I have waited'). Pushpa in short plain sentences. Bhaiyaji soft and hospitable, 'Inspector sahab', 'Tripathi ji'. Tripathi slow, very little said. names_rule holds in English: 'Inspector sahab' only from Bhaiyaji (l16, l17); the town's 'Nirala ji' first (l10); no bare 'sahab'. 'चौकी' is 'outpost' in both l17 and l34, as the bible's English has it; 'charge handover' is the same phrase in l02, l03 and l30 so her last line echoes his first.

Carried facts: every key line's fact is spoken. Set-up facts (D-004): l06 she sent them across the line; l08 the SHO has known two years and the shield is why; l09 he told neither the department nor Bhaiyaji. l17 keeps 'Cheaper than Tripathi ji, and sweeter.' (D-016 rejected cutting it). l13 is the say-it-aloud plant: 'say it aloud' is the phrase later English episodes should echo in its pay-offs (s2b01 b5, s2b02 b6, s2b03 b10, s2a01 b2).

Adaptation choices: l26 'Why didn't you join the police?' makes the Hindi 'गए' (went, meaning tried to join) explicit, and l27 says 'my chest measured one centimetre short' so an English viewer reads it as the recruitment chest measurement; l28 then turns 'chest' to courage. l18 uses the Indian-English tag 'no?' for 'ना' (the proof dropped 'na' because an English voice may misread it; 'no?' reads safely). l31 adds 'So,' as a slow, mouth-full carrier for a short turn. l12 'On record.' for 'दर्ज है'. Numbers in l12 and l20 are read digit by digit; the hyphens are for the reader and the subtitle. l10 is the same name call as the Hindi and its take may be shared.

Cue words in the shared action text that are Hindi: in b5, shot 2 starts 'from lockup में' in the Hindi; in the English cut it starts on 'the lockup'. In b2 the cut to the shield insert is on 'shield' in both cuts. In b6 shot 4 starts on the laugh tag in both.

Length (hand count, not a tool count; this session has no shell): 34 lines, dialogue about 1,234 characters with spaces and punctuation, without tags or speaker labels (1,229 before the critic rerun added ' flat' to l14); hand-count error perhaps 1 to 2 per cent. That is about 18 per cent more characters than the Hindi's 1,039 (the Hindi writer's earlier count; after the critic rerun the Hindi writer reports about 1,054 as stored, and the two counts may not use the same method), which is expected for English, and over D-016 direction 7's 1,050 if that measure is read as applying to the English cut too. It was set for Hinglish at about 9 to 10 characters a second; English is assumed (not measured here) to be spoken faster per character, so by time the English cut is shorter. Open point for S3 or the Arbiter: whether the character measure applies to English scripts, or only time does. No line was padded and none was lengthened beyond what the Hindi says.

Timing: target_seconds are set to the English length at about 11 characters a second overall (slower for Nirala, Tripathi and lines with ellipses), with a floor of 1.4 s on short turns, because Gate 0b measured real eleven_v4 takes 20 to 60 per cent over target, worst on short and emotional lines. Spoken 111.2 s + 22 speaker changes at 0.3 s (6.6 s) + silent seconds 6.8 s = 124.6 s, against 133.9 s for the Hindi (critic rerun: l14 became 'Ten minutes flat.' at 1.6 s, up from 'Ten minutes.' at 1.4 s, mirroring the Hindi 'दस minute में।'). If measured English takes run 20 per cent over these targets, the cut lands near 146 s, over the 135 s ceiling; the Hindi writer's cut order then applies to both cuts (the b11 silent hold only; the b12 hold stays at 1.8 s for receiver, two digits, one ring-back burst and the click; l12 and l20 to the bare numbers; l14 to picture; l26 into picture only with l27 reworded). Shots follow the measured voice (D-014 rule 6), so the English and Hindi cuts may differ in shot lengths.

Lines whose English target is more than 15 per cent shorter than the Hindi target (the shot will be shorter in the English cut, or held on picture): l02 (4.6 s against 5.5 s), l03 (2.6 against 3.2), l19 (2.0 against 2.4), l29 (3.0 against 3.6). Lines longer than the Hindi: l13 (5.6 against 5.0, the say-it-aloud plant, kept whole) and l27 (5.2 against 5.0); both inside 15 per cent. Every other line is within 15 per cent of its Hindi target. Overall the English spoken targets are about 8 per cent shorter (111.0 s against 120.4 s) and the cut about 7 per cent shorter.

Short turns to watch (D-006 change 22): l05 'You knew.' (9 characters), l07 'And SHO sahab?' (14), l10 'Nirala ji!' (10), l11 'Token eight.' (12), l14 'Ten minutes flat.' (17), l24 'Twenty-four.' (12), l31 'So, arrest done?' (16). Budget 3 takes each. If l05 is unstable, S10 may use 'You knew, Pushpa ji.' (she calls her 'Pushpa ji' in the bible).

Tags: unchanged from the Hindi, one per line except l17. As in the Hindi notes after the critic rerun: if the l15 take stammers or adds breaths on [nervous] or its two ellipses, S10 swaps the tag to [quietly] and keeps the text. Nothing is whispered. Nandini's loudest tag is [sharply], meaning low and fast. Nirala gets only [calm], [quietly], [earnest] and once [nervous] (l15: thin and steady, no stammer; the ellipses there are deliberate pauses).
